name: Samuel Molina
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember an old school nickname heard on the radio.” Wednesday often includes a stop at Ferris Deli, where Samuel asks for the end slice and listens to the names the counter workers use for regulars.
voice: I only knew my partner's working voice. I heard his school nickname and he sounded fourteen.
appearance: Samuel is easy to recognize by short sandy hair and a marked widow's peak and an aquiline nose and a square chin. Usually dressed in a pale blue work shirt with a copper-colored clasp that has been repaired by hand, Samuel looks toward the door whenever a name is called when listening.
personality: Samuel talks very little about private fear and recognizes it quickly in strangers. Offering a choice of seats is one of Samuel's ways of saying that it is all right to leave.
agenda: To hear the working partner's first nickname.
family: Nelson Carbone is Samuel’s cousin. Samuel brings something that can still be enjoyed tomorrow. Nelson checks the date twice. Arrangements do change in their family. Taking a delay seriously without treating it as an insult took both of them years. Asked about *The sheltered corner*, Nelson says, “I sell coffee on the old corner. My first customer is now a pensioner who only comes to talk.”
connections: Teresa Lopez. A uniform and a school nickname briefly belong to the same young-looking person.

reactions.response: Samuel gives the expected speaker a seat and lets the old classmates start talking amongst themselves.
